cleared.check: Transient storage lifetime and slot read order in bor v2.11.2 ParallelStateDB, the BlockSTM V2 worker state, read as source.
cleared.result: Each transaction gets a new transient store in Prepare (parallel_statedb.go:1277-1279) and a recycled worker clears it (line 272), so the unlock flag at src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25 and the deltas at src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39 cannot pass from one transaction to the next in a parallel block. Persistent reads take the worker's own write first, then the highest lower writer in the MVStore unless a later SuicidePath write wiped the account, then base state, and every answer is recorded for validation (lines 332-349, 597-620, 967-1034); validateOne re-executes a transaction whose read set went stale (v2_executor.go:629-660). A parallel result that differed from serial order would also give another state root than the serial importers, which is a fork and not a silent change of pool state.

leadResults.answer: Today the oldest release that can follow BNB Chain mainnet is v1.7.7, which scheduled Pasteur (2026-08-25, the last activated fork); v1.7.8 is a maintenance release. Both are below v1.8.0 and still carry the superinstruction feature behind --vm.opcode.optimize, off by default. v1.8.0-alpha removed it entirely (PR 3759) and leaves the flag inert with a warning. Jenner at 2026-12-08 02:30 UTC is mandatory for every mainnet operator and only v1.8.2 schedules it on mainnet (v1.8.1 is for Chapel only), so from that moment every node that follows mainnet runs code without fused instructions. Until then a validator that opted into the feature on v1.7.7 or v1.7.8 would carry the v1.7.1 and v1.7.3 fixes, and a wrong word in a block it produced would give a different state root and be rejected by the other validators, so it cannot change pool state silently. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/develop/CHANGELOG.md lines 3-30, 31-35, 97-136, 154-168.

The binary run with non-empty MVStore answers was not done. Reading bor v2.11.2 core/state/parallel_statedb.go: readStoreWait (lines 332-349) returns a committed lower writer at once, waits on an ESTIMATE entry through handleEstimate (383-392) and retries, GetState (967-1001) and GetCommittedState (1003-1034) apply a lower write only when its writer index is above the latest SuicidePath writer from priorDestructedAt (597-620), and every answer is recorded for validation; transient storage is fresh per transaction (1277-1279). The order matches serial semantics as read, and a divergence would give another state root than serial importers. The lead stays open for the run it asks for.

For BNB Chain the pocket gateway now serves historical traces from part of its backends (Geth v1.8.2-54afaff4 and v1.7.8), and a retry loop reads them. Of the 5,726 window transactions without a cycle 24 trace a first batch was traced and replayed through the cycle 23 model: txs 395, words compared 9348, transactions with a mismatch 0, blocks [135822015, 135831839]; backends around them: Geth/v1.7.8/linux-amd64/go1.25.12 (310), Geth/v1.8.2-54afaff4-20261103/linux-amd64/go1.25.14 (217), Geth/v1.8.2/linux-amd64/go1.26.10 (182), reth-bsc/v0.1.4-hotfix-23b510f/linux (65), reth-bsc/v0.1.2-968d07d/linux (16). Blastapi (free tier refuses), 1rpc (method not allowed), meowrpc (method absent), blxrbdn (403), nodies, blockpi and ankr (keys or paid plans) still serve no trace. The rest of the window remains to be traced; the Avalanche part was closed in cycle 32.
